newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea blasts Seoul plan to build refugee camp.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea blasts Seoul plan to build refugee camp.

text.p: North Korea on Wednesday slammed South Korea's plans to build a camp for northern refugees, saying it would be an anti-Pyongyang spy base filled with "human rubbish" wanted for crimes in the North.

Seoul's plan to begin constructing a camp next year "is aimed at building an anti-communist base for the human rubbish who defected to the south after committing crimes in the northern half of Korea and thus encouraging distrust and confrontation", North Korea's official media said.
On December 6, South Korea's Unification Ministry said Seoul would build its first camp, capable of holding up to 500 people, to cope with a possible exodus from the communist North.
The announcement came after 17 North Koreans -- 16 members of one family and a security guard -- fled to South Korea through China and Hong Kong in the biggest-ever single flight from North Korea.
The refugee arrival set off alarm bells in Seoul that the North's deteriorating food and economic situation might soon become so dire that there would be a mass exodus.

The Unification Ministry's North Korean counterpart lambasted the plan as "an undisguised challenge to our people and an anti-North provocation for vicious political purposes", the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) reported.

"Those whom they call 'defectors from the North' are not refugees. They are human rubbish who fled to the South after committing indelible crimes including murder and robbery," said Pyongyang's Committee for the Peaceful Reunification of the Fatherland in a statement carried on KCNA.
North Korea, which brands all defectors as criminals, told Seoul to scrap the camp plan or face the consequences of Pyongyang's policy of "punishing provokers".

On Tuesday, Choi Young-ho, a North Korean border guard who guided 16 other defectors into China on their way to South Korea, told a news conference in Seoul the North had nearly tripled the number of guards on its border with China.

The 17, the biggest group of escapees since the 1950-53 Korean War, brought to 51 the number of defectors to South Korea this year. Last year, 38 made it across the border and in 1994 a total of 50 landed.
South and North Korea remain technically at war since their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce, not a peace pact.

International relief agencies report peasants in the North scrounging for tree bark, grass and edible roots in their search for food because of the failure of crops for two years running after heavy rain and floods.
